pr_title: Add basic support for user subuid/subgid management.
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

Fixes #68199 

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
user

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

This addition does not support arbitrary static assignments of subuid or subgid, but does support ensuring that a range is present for a user.

For example:

```
- name: set subid for gordon
  user: name=gordon subuid=present subgid=present
```

> This addition does not support arbitrary static assignments of subuid or subgid, but does support ensuring that a range is present for a user.

I think this is by far the most common (and useful) use-case. I don't think many people will care that the exact ranges aren't deterministic.

The only thing I'm worried about is `65536`. Is this the default for all Linux OS'es? Can we retrieve this value from the OS in case the user (or the OS) changed this default?
65536 is used as a default value in case login.defs does not specify a count.  The block immediately following that value will load the values for min, max, and count sub-ids from login.defs.
The min, max, and count values should be parameters as well. This also needs integration tests and a changelog.

The integration test will need a little more work.  For systems that support subuid and subgid, ranges are assigned automatically when users are added.  Currently only "subuid: present" is supported, and I expect that the module will have to add support for at least "subuid: absent" in order to get meaningful test results.

@samdoran Integration tests and changelog have been added.

I'm not sure it makes sense to add min/max/count as user-specified values, since those are system-dependent values loaded from /etc/login.defs.

As for the rationale behind this implementation:  Systems that support subuid and subgid will assign such a range when new local users are created.  However, systems that use non-local users (such as FreeIPA) do not currently have a centralized means of distributing or assigning such ranges.  Those features are being discussed upstream, but there is no ETA for an implementation.  In the mean time, indefinitely, organizations with central user management which want to use rootless containers must assign subuid/subgid ranges on each system individually.

This implementation follows the default behavior of useradd, assigning a subuid range for users based on the values specified in login.defs.

The underlying system supports storing multiple ranges in the subuid/subgid file, so in order to properly support the specification of arbitrary static ranges in an Ansible playbook, the user module would need to be able to detect overlap and intersection with the existing specification which might provide multiple ranges.  I believe this would involve rather a lot of code in addition to the patch that I've proposed in order to correctly provide an idempotent module.  I don't think the value of that addition justifies the effort that would be required.  For my own purposes, I only need to ensure that non-local users have a range that's consistent with the range that would be added if they had been created as a local user.
We are facing this issue too. Is there anything which we can do to move this along?

Hi!

Thanks very much for your submission to Ansible.  It means a lot to us that you've taken time to contribute.

Unfortunately, we're not sure if we want this feature in the program, and I don't want this to seem confrontational.
Our reasons for this are:

   * The user module is already complex as it is, we don't wish to overload it with more options that are specific to certain platforms
   * We recommend you either keep a copy of these changes in your own collection or create a module specifically for subuid/subgid management rather than trying to add it into one module that rules them all

However, we're absolutely always up for discussion.
Because this project is very active, we're unlikely to see comments made on closed tickets and we lock them after some time.
If you or anyone else has any further questions, please let us know by using any of the communication methods listed in the page below:

   * https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/community/communication.html

In the future, sometimes starting a discussion on the development list prior to implementing a feature can make getting things included a little easier, but it's not always necessary.

Thank you once again for this and your interest in Ansible!

issue_context.title: Add support for subuid and subgid to user module
issue_context.body:
<!--- Verify first that your feature was not already discussed on GitHub -->
<!--- Complete *all* sections as described, this form is processed automatically -->

##### SUMMARY
Subuid's and subgid's are used as part of Linux user namespaces. Heavily relied on by container technologies such as podman/docker.

Adding subuid and subgid support in the user module would make this easier.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Idea

##### COMPONENT NAME
The ansible user module

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The usermod command supports the following:
```
usermod --add-subuids 200000-201000 --add-subgids 200000-201000 johndoe
```

This results in a corresponding entry in `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid`
```
johndoe:200000:1000
```
<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->

It could possibly look, like either this:
```yaml
- name: Add the user 'johndoe' with a specific uid and a primary group of 'admin'
  user:
    name: johndoe
    comment: John Doe
    uid: 1001
    group: admin
    subuids: 200000-201000
    subgids: 200000-201000
```
or this:
```yaml
- name: Add the user 'johndoe' with a specific uid and a primary group of 'admin'
  user:
    name: johndoe
    comment: John Doe
    uid: 1001
    group: admin
    subuid: 200000:1000
    subgid: 200000:1000
```
Depending on why you're using it, there may need to be a handler run to execute some commands, similar to the systemd daemon needing a reload after modifying a service file.  I'm just not 100% sure on what all the possible combinations of a user task being "changed" are that would require this handler to be triggered.  IE, updating a comment or group would not.

> The usermod command supports the following:
> `usermod --add-subuids 200000-201000 --add-subgids 200000-201000 johndoe`
> This results in a corresponding entry in /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid
> `johndoe:200000:1000`

The example is wrong. This would result in `johndoe:200000:1001`

To achive `johndoe:200000:1000` you need to specify `--add-subuids 200000-200999` which looks like the following with the first option:
```
subuids: 200000-200999
subgids: 200000-200999
```

Therefore I would vote for the second option:
```
subuid: 200000:1000
subgid: 200000:1000
 ```

Overall, I find it very tedious that subuids and subgids have to be specified by start + count, which makes them hard to use if the set of users is not fixed in time. It would be nice if ansible would provide a higher-level interface in which it would be possible to specify just user and number of sub{u,g}id-s for this uses – ansible would then check if this is already assigned and if needed find the range to use.

How about allowing different ways to specify them?

With start and count:
```.yaml
  subuids:
    start: 100000
    count: 65536
```
With start and end:
```.yaml
  subuids:
    start: 100000
    end: 165535
```
Just a count (Ansible will pick a start so it fits):
```.yaml
  subuids:
    count: 65536
```

(Same possibilities would apply to `subguids`.)
